text: "Are You Kidding? I Pled Guilty To Solicitation of Prostitution" | Epstein Testimony Released | N18GThe latest release of files related to the US Department of Justice investigation into Jeffrey Epstein includes a one-and-a-half-hour video deposition in February 2010 related to a 2008 lawsuit brought by a plaintiff, referred to as L.M., alleging she was abused by the convicted sexual offender while still a minor. In the video, Epstein is questioned by Brad Edwards, an attorney for L.M. Additionally, Michael Pike, an attorney for Epstein, is also heard raising objections throughout the video. 'I must assert my Sixth Amendment, Fourteenth Amendment, and Fifth Amendment rights under the Mrs.5 Constitution.' The speaker repeatedly cites legal advice when pressed for answers regarding criminal charges allegedly involving solicitation of prostitution. Despite persistent lines of questioning focused on whether underage minor females were involved and the methods of procuring them, direct answers to specific inquiries are withheld on the grounds of constitutional rights, legal process, and attorney advice. The dialogue includes multiple objections and calls to strike as the jury is provided limited information about the legal case, with the speaker regularly reaffirming the right not to answer questions related to the charges or underlying facts. The transcript further touches on allegations by attorneys referenced as 'Mr. Edwards and Mr. Jaffe,' with claims about the crafting of malicious cases and situations described as fraudulent schemes in South Florida; these claims are also met with resistance and reliance on the assertion of amendments. Emphasis is given to the distinction between ‘solicitation of prostitution’ and ‘underage prostitution,’ reiterating that the guilty plea was for the former, while declining to elaborate further. Across the exchange, the speaker signals a consistent refusal to engage on potentially incriminating topics, continuously invoking constitutional protections as justification for not responding to questions about alleged misconduct and litigation specifics. #epsteinfiles #jeffreyepstein #departmentofjustice #usatoday #epsteinlist #cnbctv18
